data.title: Lysosomal recruitment of TSC2 is a universal response to cellular stress
data.authors: Demetriades C; Teleman AA et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: Lysosomal recruitment of TSC2 is a universal response to cellular stress that inhibits mTORC1.
data.abstract_excerpt: mTORC1 promotes cell growth and is therefore inactivated upon unfavourable growth conditions. Signalling pathways downstream of most cellular stresses converge on TSC1/2, which serves as an integration point that inhibits mTORC1. The TSC1/2 complex was shown to translocate to lysosomes to inactivate mTORC1 in response to two stresses: amino-acid starvation and growth factor removal. Whether other stresses also regulate TSC2 localization is not known. How TSC2 localization responds to combinations of stresses and other stimuli is also unknown.

extracted_findings.intervention: Various cellular stresses (amino-acid/growth-factor withdrawal, etc.) – mechanistic
extracted_findings.effect: Diverse stresses relocate TSC2 to the lysosome → inhibit mTORC1 (a universal response)
